ai.description: This small skink reaches 4–5 cm in snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and possesses fused, transparent eyelids. It belongs to the family Scincidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ablepharus sikimmensis* is best distinguished by its lack of visible eyelids, giving it a permanent "staring" expression, unlike the movable eyelids found in most other skinks.
ai.habitat: The Sikkim Ground Skink inhabits moist, leaf-littered floors of temperate broadleaf and coniferous forests at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters in the Himalayas.
ai.behavior: The Sikkim Ground Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and damp forest floors during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ablepharus sikimmensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sikkim Ground Skink inhabits the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
